calls.thesis: Bullish coverage of a held name (owned for both AI chips and networking): revenue +36.5% YoY, custom XPU plus XPU-attach (scale-up fabrics, memory, CXL, co-processors) market expected to more than double by fiscal 2028 per its investor day, and 1.6T/scale-out switching growth — while noting it is one of the more expensive names here at a forward FY27 P/E of ~49.

Reiterated BUY: 'I've been buying Marvell now for a while' — one of the only competitors to Broadcom in custom AI accelerators; Nvidia's $2B investment + NVLink partnership brings a competitor into its own ecosystem, and he likes both sides of that opportunity.

Reiterated BUY: Microsoft's Maia 300 is believed to be part of the Marvell ecosystem, bullish for Marvell as it expands in ASICs (high production from 2027); Nvidia's 576-GPU scale-up/scale-out networking news is also very bullish for Marvell.
calls.price_at_call: down ~3% on the day (no level stated)

calls.thesis: FLIP from UNCERTAIN (Oct 5): now one of his favorite AI stocks and a key accelerator-chip player vs NVDA; Nvidia bringing Marvell into its own ecosystem adds to the case.
Marvell investor day: FY2028 revenue outlook raised to ~$20B, $30 EPS guided for CY2030; at a 30x PE that implies a potential ~$600 stock price.
calls.base: FY2028 guide raised $18B->$20B (from $16.5B two quarters prior), driven by networking/scale-up-scale-out; custom silicon FY2029 target >$12B vs $10B+; data-center revenue $18B FY2028, target pulled a year early.
calls.bull: FY2031 model $70-90B revenue implying >$30 non-GAAP EPS at midpoint; he argues management is conservative and real numbers could be much higher.
calls.bear: Numbers are 4-5 years out ('blurriness'); new technologies/networking solutions could end the thesis; no sure thing in this space.
